decisions.reason: Job is so thin that his bones seem stuck to his skin (Psalm 102:6; Lamentations 4:8).

decisions.choice: escaped with the skin of my teeth: barely alive
alternatives: escaped with nothing but my gums
decisions.reason: The phrase is unique and hard. It most likely means that Job has escaped with almost nothing, barely alive. Since teeth have no skin, some think of the gums. The whole line may also be ironic: all he has left is what does not exist.

decisions.choice: I am nothing but skin and bones. I am barely alive.
alternatives: my bone clings to my skin; I have escaped with the skin of my teeth
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the two pictures (m1, m2).

decisions.choice: "이의 가죽" (the skin of my teeth), kept as the picture
decisions.reason: The phrase is unique and its sense uncertain (meaning decision m2); Literal and Balanced keep the strange picture, as the English does, and Readable says what it most likely means.

decisions.choice: "escapei com a pele dos meus dentes" (L), "escapei só com a pele dos meus dentes" (B); "Estou vivo por um fio" (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase is unique and its sense uncertain (m2), so Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew picture, as the English does, rather than replace it with a Portuguese idiom that would settle the meaning; Balanced adds "só" as the English adds "only". Readable gives the most likely sense with the everyday "por um fio".

decisions.choice: "दाँतों की खाल लेकर बच निकला हूँ"
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew picture (m2), as the English does; Hindi "बाल-बाल बचना" says the same thing with another picture, and Readable gives the plain sense.

decisions.choice: "с кожей моих зубов"
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the Hebrew picture, which has no Russian idiom; Readable says what it means, barely alive (m2).

source.text: חָנֻּ֬נִי חָנֻּ֣נִי אַתֶּ֣ם רֵעָ֑י כִּ֥י יַד־אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַּ נָ֣גְעָה בִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Have pity on me, have pity on me, you my friends, for the hand of God has touched me.

en.L: Have pity on me, have pity on me, you my friends, \q for the hand of God has struck me.
en.B: Have pity on me, have pity on me, you my friends, \q for the hand of God has struck me.
en.R: Have pity on me, my friends, please have pity on me! \q God has struck me down.

es.L: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} piedad de mí, {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} piedad de mí, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, amigos míos, \q porque la mano de Dios me ha herido.
es.B: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} compasión de mí, {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} compasión de mí, amigos míos, \q porque la mano de Dios me ha golpeado.
es.R: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} compasión de mí, amigos míos, ¡por favor, {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} compasión de mí! \q Dios me ha derribado.

fr.L: Ayez pitié de moi, ayez pitié de moi, vous, mes amis, \q car la main de Dieu m’a frappé.
fr.B: Prenez pitié de moi, prenez pitié de moi, vous mes amis, \q car la main de Dieu m’a frappé.
fr.R: Ayez pitié de moi, mes amis, je vous en prie, ayez pitié de moi ! \q Dieu m’a frappé et m’a jeté à terre.

sw.L: Nihurumieni, nihurumieni, ninyi rafiki zangu, \q kwa maana mkono wa Mungu umenipiga.
sw.B: Nioneeni huruma, nioneeni huruma, enyi rafiki zangu, \q kwa maana mkono wa Mungu umenipiga.
sw.R: Nihurumieni, rafiki zangu, tafadhali nihurumieni! \q Mungu amenipiga na kuniangusha.

vi.L: Hãy thương xót tôi, hãy thương xót tôi, hỡi các anh là bạn tôi, \q vì tay Đức Chúa Trời đã đánh tôi.
vi.B: Xin thương xót tôi, xin thương xót tôi, hỡi các bạn của tôi, \q vì bàn tay Đức Chúa Trời đã giáng trên tôi.
vi.R: Các bạn ơi, xin thương xót tôi, xin hãy thương xót tôi! \q Đức Chúa Trời đã đánh gục tôi.

ko.L: 나를 불쌍히 여기시오, 나를 불쌍히 여기시오, 그대들 나의 친구들이여, \q 하나님의 손이 나를 치셨소.
ko.B: 나를 불쌍히 여기시오, 나를 불쌍히 여기시오, 내 친구들이여, \q 하나님의 손이 나를 치셨기 때문이오.
ko.R: 친구들이여, 나를 불쌍히 여겨 주시오. 제발 나를 불쌍히 여겨 주시오! \q 하나님께서 나를 쳐서 쓰러뜨리셨소.

pt.L: Tenham piedade de mim, tenham piedade de mim, vocês, meus amigos, \q pois a mão de Deus me feriu.
pt.B: Tenham compaixão de mim, tenham compaixão de mim, vocês, meus amigos, \q pois a mão de Deus me atingiu.
pt.R: Tenham pena de mim, meus amigos, por favor, tenham pena de mim! \q Deus me derrubou.

am.L: ራሩልኝ፤ ራሩልኝ፤ እናንተ ወዳጆቼ፤ \q የአምላክ እጅ መታችኝና።
am.B: ራሩልኝ፣ ራሩልኝ፣ እናንተ ወዳጆቼ፤ \q የአምላክ እጅ መትታኛለችና።
am.R: ወዳጆቼ ሆይ፣ ራሩልኝ፤ እባካችሁ ራሩልኝ! \q አምላክ መትቶኛል።

hi.L: मुझ पर दया करो, मुझ पर दया करो, हे मेरे मित्रो, \q क्योंकि परमेश्वर के हाथ ने मुझे मारा है।
hi.B: मुझ पर दया करो, मुझ पर दया करो, हे मेरे मित्रो, \q क्योंकि परमेश्वर के हाथ ने मुझ पर वार किया है।
hi.R: हे मेरे दोस्तो, मुझ पर दया करो, कृपया मुझ पर दया करो! \q परमेश्वर ने मुझे मार गिराया है।

ru.L: Помилуйте меня, помилуйте меня вы, мои друзья, \q потому что рука Бога поразила меня.
ru.B: Сжальтесь надо мной, сжальтесь надо мной, вы, мои друзья, \q ведь рука Бога поразила меня.
ru.R: Пожалейте меня, друзья мои, пожалейте же меня! \q Бог поразил меня.

ja.L: わたしをあわれんでくれ、わたしをあわれんでくれ、あなたがた、わたしの友よ。 \q 神の手がわたしを打たれたのだから。
ja.B: あわれんでくれ、あわれんでくれ、わたしの友よ。 \q 神の手がわたしを打たれたのだ。
ja.R: 友よ、わたしをあわれんでくれ、どうかあわれんでくれ！ \q 神が、わたしを打ち倒されたのだ。

uk.L: Змилуйтеся наді мною, змилуйтеся наді мною, ви, мої друзі, \q бо рука Бога вразила мене.
uk.B: Змилуйтеся наді мною, змилуйтеся наді мною, ви, мої друзі, \q бо рука Бога вразила мене.
uk.R: Змилуйтеся наді мною, мої друзі, прошу, змилуйтеся наді мною! \q Бог мене вразив.

decisions.choice: the hand of God has touched me: as the Accuser proposed
decisions.reason: The verb (naga') is the one used when the Accuser asked God to "stretch out your hand and touch" Job's possessions and body (1:11; 2:5). To be touched by God's hand is to be struck by him (1 Samuel 6:9).

decisions.choice: have pity: show grace, be kind
decisions.reason: The verb (chanan) means to show favor or mercy. Job, who has accused the friends, now begs them for kindness.

decisions.choice: struck
decisions.reason: "Touched" is too gentle in English for what the verb means here (m1).

decisions.choice: Job's plea to the friends "あわれんでくれ" (plain request)
decisions.reason: Job book convention (JOB-1 notes, 6:24-29): Job's requests to the friends are plain "〜てくれ".

source.text: לָ֭מָּה תִּרְדְּפֻ֣נִי כְמוֹ־אֵ֑ל וּ֝מִבְּשָׂרִ֗י לֹ֣א תִשְׂבָּֽעוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Why do you pursue me like God, and from my flesh not are you satisfied?

en.L: Why do you pursue me as God [does], \q and are not satisfied with my flesh?
en.B: Why do you hound me as God does? \q Will you never have enough of my flesh?
en.R: Why do you chase after me the way God does? \q Have you not hurt me enough already?

es.L: ¿Por qué me {{plural_you:persiguen|perseguís}} como Dios, \q y no {{plural_you:se sacian|os saciáis}} de mi carne?
es.B: ¿Por qué me {{plural_you:acosan|acosáis}} como lo hace Dios? \q ¿Nunca {{plural_you:se hartarán|os hartaréis}} de mi carne?
es.R: ¿Por qué me {{plural_you:persiguen|perseguís}} como lo hace Dios? \q ¿Todavía no me {{plural_you:han|habéis}} hecho bastante daño?

fr.L: Pourquoi me poursuivez-vous comme Dieu [le fait], \q et n’êtes-vous pas rassasiés de ma chair ?
fr.B: Pourquoi me traquez-vous comme Dieu le fait ? \q N’aurez-vous jamais assez de ma chair ?
fr.R: Pourquoi me pourchassez-vous comme Dieu le fait ? \q Ne m’avez-vous pas déjà fait assez de mal ?

sw.L: Mbona mnanifuatia kama Mungu [afanyavyo], \q wala hamshibi nyama yangu?
sw.B: Kwa nini mnaniwinda kama Mungu afanyavyo? \q Je, hamtatosheka kamwe na nyama yangu?
sw.R: Kwa nini mnanikimbiza kama Mungu anavyofanya? \q Je, bado hamjaniumiza vya kutosha?

vi.L: Sao các anh bắt bớ tôi như Đức Chúa Trời [vậy], \q và không chán thịt tôi?
vi.B: Sao các anh truy đuổi tôi như Đức Chúa Trời làm? \q Các anh ăn thịt tôi chưa đủ sao?
vi.R: Sao các anh đuổi theo tôi như Đức Chúa Trời đuổi theo tôi? \q Các anh làm tôi đau khổ vẫn chưa đủ sao?

ko.L: 어찌하여 그대들은 하나님처럼 나를 쫓으며, \q 내 살로도 배부르지 않소?
ko.B: 어찌하여 그대들은 하나님처럼 나를 몰아붙이오? \q 내 살을 뜯고도 아직 성에 차지 않소?
ko.R: 왜 그대들은 하나님처럼 나를 쫓아다니오? \q 나를 이만큼 괴롭혔으면 충분하지 않소?

pt.L: Por que vocês me perseguem como Deus [faz] \q e não se fartam da minha carne?
pt.B: Por que vocês me acossam como Deus faz? \q Nunca vão se fartar da minha carne?
pt.R: Por que vocês correm atrás de mim como Deus faz? \q Ainda não me machucaram o bastante?

am.L: እንደ እግዚአብሔር ስለ ምን ታሳድዱኛላችሁ? \q ከሥጋዬስ አትጠግቡምን?
am.B: እግዚአብሔር እንደሚያደርገው ለምን ታሳድዱኛላችሁ? \q ሥጋዬን መቦጨቅ ከቶ አትጠግቡምን?
am.R: እግዚአብሔር እንደሚያሳድደኝ እናንተስ ለምን ታሳድዱኛላችሁ? \q እስካሁን የጎዳችሁኝ አይበቃችሁም?

hi.L: तुम परमेश्वर की तरह मेरा पीछा क्यों करते हो, \q और मेरे मांस से तृप्त नहीं होते?
hi.B: तुम परमेश्वर की तरह मेरे पीछे क्यों पड़े हो? \q क्या मेरे मांस से तुम्हारा जी कभी नहीं भरेगा?
hi.R: तुम भी परमेश्वर की तरह मेरे पीछे क्यों पड़े हो? \q क्या तुमने मुझे अब तक काफ़ी चोट नहीं पहुँचाई?

ru.L: Зачем вы преследуете меня, как Бог, \q и плотью моей не насыщаетесь?
ru.B: Зачем вы гонитесь за мной, как Бог? \q Неужели вам мало моей плоти?
ru.R: Почему вы гонитесь за мной так же, как Бог? \q Разве вы ещё недостаточно меня измучили?

ja.L: なぜ、あなたがたは神のようにわたしを追い、 \q わたしの肉に満足しないのか？
ja.B: なぜ、あなたがたは神がなさるように、わたしを追い詰めるのか？ \q わたしの肉を、いつまでも食い足りないのか？
ja.R: なぜ、あなたたちは、神のようにわたしを追い回すのか？ \q わたしを、もう十分苦しめたではないか？

uk.L: Чому ви переслідуєте мене, як Бог, \q і не насичуєтеся моїм тілом?
uk.B: Чому ви цькуєте мене, як Бог? \q Невже вам ніколи не досить мого тіла?
uk.R: Чому ви женетеся за мною так, як Бог? \q Хіба ви ще не досить мене скривдили?

decisions.choice: as God: the word 'El
decisions.reason: Job compares the friends to God, who is pursuing him (verses 6-12). It could also be read "like a god", playing God; the comparison is the same.

decisions.choice: not satisfied with my flesh: you keep tearing at me
decisions.reason: The friends are pictured as wild beasts that cannot get enough of his flesh (Psalm 27:2). In Aramaic, to "eat someone's pieces" means to slander them (Daniel 3:8), and that may be in view: they keep attacking him with accusations.

decisions.choice: Have you not hurt me enough already?
alternatives: are you not satisfied with my flesh?

records.literal_gloss: Who will give then that would be written my words? Who will give [that] in a scroll they would be inscribed?

en.L: Oh that my words were written down! \q Oh that they were inscribed in a scroll!
en.B: Oh, that my words were written down, \q that they were inscribed on a scroll,
en.R: I wish someone would write down what I am saying. \q I wish someone would write it on a scroll.

es.L: ¡Oh, si mis palabras fueran escritas! \q ¡Oh, si fueran grabadas en un rollo!
es.B: ¡Ojalá mis palabras quedaran escritas, \q ojalá fueran grabadas en un rollo,
es.R: Quisiera que alguien escribiera lo que digo. \q Quisiera que alguien lo escribiera en un rollo.

fr.L: Oh ! que mes paroles soient donc écrites ! \q Oh ! qu’elles soient gravées dans un rouleau !
fr.B: Si seulement mes paroles étaient écrites, \q si seulement elles étaient gravées dans un rouleau,
fr.R: Je voudrais que quelqu’un écrive ce que je dis. \q Je voudrais que quelqu’un l’écrive dans un rouleau.

sw.L: Laiti maneno yangu yangeandikwa! \q Laiti yangechorwa katika gombo!
sw.B: Laiti maneno yangu yangeandikwa, \q laiti yangechorwa katika gombo,
sw.R: Natamani mtu angeandika ninayosema. \q Natamani mtu angeyaandika katika gombo.

vi.L: Ôi, ước gì lời tôi được chép lại! \q Ôi, ước gì chúng được khắc vào cuộn sách!
vi.B: Ước gì lời tôi được ghi chép lại, \q ước gì chúng được khắc vào một cuộn sách,
vi.R: Tôi ước có ai đó chép lại những điều tôi nói. \q Tôi ước có ai đó viết chúng vào một cuộn sách.

ko.L: 오, 내 말이 기록되었으면! \q 오, 그것이 두루마리에 새겨졌으면!
ko.B: 내 말이 글로 기록되었으면, \q 두루마리에 새겨졌으면,
ko.R: 누군가 내가 하는 말을 받아 적어 주면 좋겠다. \q 누군가 그것을 두루마리에 적어 주면 좋겠다.

pt.L: Ah, se as minhas palavras fossem escritas! \q Ah, se fossem gravadas num rolo!
pt.B: Ah, se alguém escrevesse as minhas palavras, \q se as registrasse num rolo,
pt.R: Eu queria que alguém escrevesse o que estou dizendo. \q Queria que alguém escrevesse isso num rolo.

am.L: ምነው ቃሌ ቢጻፍ! \q ምነው በጥቅልል መጽሐፍ ቢቀረጽ!
am.B: ምነው ቃሌ በተጻፈ፣ \q በጥቅልል መጽሐፍም በተቀረጸ፣
am.R: ምነው አንድ ሰው የምናገረውን ቢጽፈው! \q ምነው በጥቅልል መጽሐፍ ላይ ቢጽፈው!

hi.L: काश, मेरे शब्द लिख लिए जाते! \q काश, वे किसी पुस्तक में अंकित किए जाते!
hi.B: काश, मेरी बातें लिख ली जातीं, \q काश, वे किसी पुस्तक में अंकित की जातीं,
hi.R: काश, कोई मेरी कही बातें लिख लेता। \q काश, कोई उन्हें एक पुस्तक में लिख देता।

ru.L: О, если бы записаны были мои слова! \q О, если бы они были начертаны в свитке!
ru.B: О, если бы мои слова были записаны, \q если бы их начертали в свитке,
ru.R: Как бы мне хотелось, чтобы кто-нибудь записал то, что я говорю. \q Как бы хотелось, чтобы это записали в свиток.

ja.L: ああ、わたしの言葉が書き留められればよいのに！ \q ああ、それが書物に刻まれればよいのに！
ja.B: ああ、わたしの言葉が書き記され、 \q 巻物に刻みつけられ、
ja.R: だれかが、わたしの言うことを書き留めてくれたらいいのに。 \q 巻物に書き記してくれたらいいのに。

uk.L: О, якби мої слова були записані! \q О, якби вони були накреслені в сувої!
uk.B: О, якби мої слова були записані, \q якби їх накреслили в сувої,
uk.R: Я хотів би, щоб хтось записав те, що я кажу. \q Я хотів би, щоб хтось записав це в сувій.

decisions.choice: who will give: oh that, if only
decisions.reason: "Who will give?" is the Hebrew way of saying "if only" or "oh that" (6:8; 11:5; 14:4, 13).

decisions.choice: a scroll: a written record, an inscription
decisions.reason: The word (sefer) means any written document, a scroll or an inscription. Job wants his words kept as a lasting record for a future hearing.

decisions.choice: Oh that (L, B), I wish (R)
decisions.reason: The levels give the meaning of the idiom (m1).

decisions.choice: "काश"
decisions.reason: "Who will give" is the Hebrew way of saying a wish (m1); every level uses the Hindi wish-word "काश", as the English uses "Oh that" and "I wish". "पुस्तक" is a scroll here, a written record.

records.literal_gloss: With a stylus of iron and lead, forever in the rock they would be engraved!

en.L: with an iron stylus and lead, \q forever engraved in the rock!
en.B: with an iron chisel and with lead, \q carved in the rock forever!
en.R: I wish my words could be carved into rock with an iron tool \q and filled in with lead, so that they would last forever.

es.B: con cincel de hierro y con plomo, \q grabadas en la roca para siempre!

decisions.choice: Redeemer (go'el): the next of kin who stands up for a family member
decisions.reason: The go'el was the nearest relative, whose duty was to buy back a family member's land (Leviticus 25:25), buy him out of slavery (Leviticus 25:48-49), avenge his death (Numbers 35:19), keep his name alive (Ruth 3-4), and defend the helpless in court (Proverbs 23:10-11; Jeremiah 50:34). Job's own family has abandoned him (verses 13-19), yet he is sure that someone will take up his cause.

decisions.choice: who the Redeemer is: most likely God himself
alternatives: a heavenly defender who pleads Job's case before God
decisions.reason: Job does not name his Redeemer. In verses 26-27 he says he will see God, which suggests that God himself will at last stand up for Job, even though Job feels God is now his attacker (verses 6-12). God is often called Israel's Redeemer (Psalm 19:15; Isaiah 41:14; 47:4). Others think of a heavenly figure distinct from God, like the witness in heaven Job spoke of (16:19-21) or the go-between he longed for (9:33; 33:23). Christian tradition has long heard in this verse the hope of a living Redeemer and of resurrection; the text itself leaves the figure unnamed.

decisions.choice: at the last: in the end, or as the last one
alternatives: as the one who has the last word
decisions.reason: The word ('acharon) means "last". It can mean "at last", in the end, or describe the Redeemer as the last to speak, the one who has the final say in Job's case.

decisions.choice: stand upon the dust: rise to speak in court, on the earth or over Job's grave
decisions.reason: "Stand up" is used of a witness or advocate rising to speak in court (Deuteronomy 19:15-16; Psalm 12:6). "The dust" can be the earth (41:25) or the dust of the grave where Job will lie (7:21; 17:16).

decisions.choice: Redeemer (L, B); the one who will defend me (my Redeemer), will stand up for me (R)
decisions.reason: "Redeemer" keeps the family duty of the go'el (m1) and the link with God as Redeemer (m2). Readable says what the Redeemer will do, "the one who will defend me", keeps the word in brackets, and adds "for me" to show that he stands up in Job's defense (m4).

decisions.choice: he with the deity_pronoun setting
decisions.reason: The pronoun follows the most likely reading, that the Redeemer is God (m2); see the footnote for the other view.

decisions.choice: "al término" (L), "en el último momento" (B), "se pondrá en pie"
decisions.reason: The words follow the gloss: "last" may mean "at last" or "as the last one" (meaning decision m3), and "stand" is the advocate rising in court (m4). The Spanish avoids the familiar wording of the older Spanish versions; a reviewer should check the line reads well.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun on "il" for the Redeemer
decisions.reason: As the English (decision r-en-2), the pronoun follows the most likely reading, that the Redeemer is God himself (meaning decision m2); the footnote gives the other view.

decisions.choice: "Mkombozi" with the deity_pronoun span on the free pronoun "yeye"
decisions.reason: "Mkombozi" keeps the family duty of buying back that the go'el carried (meaning decision m1) and the link with God as Redeemer; Readable says "yule atakayenitetea" and keeps "Mkombozi wangu" in brackets, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "tôi" for Job, and "Ngài" with the span for the Redeemer
decisions.reason: Job is speaking to his friends here, not to God, so he says "tôi"; the Redeemer is "Ngài" because the most likely reading is that he is God (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "살아 계신다", "서실", with the honorific and no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Korean has no deity_pronoun spans; the honorific -시- carries the reading that the Redeemer is God (meaning decision m2), as the English span does. If the other view were taken, the honorific would still suit a heavenly defender.

decisions.choice: "o meu redentor" (L, B); "aquele que vai me defender (o meu redentor)" (R)
decisions.reason: The go'el is the next of kin who buys back land and freedom, avenges blood and defends a relative in court (m1). Leviticus 25:25 and Ruth call that relative "o resgatador" in Portuguese; here Job applies the same word to the one who will take up his cause, and "redentor" is the noun of the same family duty that Portuguese uses where God is the go'el of his people (Isaiah 41:14), the most likely reading of this verse (m2). "Defensor" would keep only the courtroom side and "vingador" only the blood-feud side. Readable says what he will do, as the English does, and keeps "o meu redentor" in brackets. The line is drafted from the gloss: "se erguerá sobre o pó" keeps the Hebrew "dust" (m4) where familiar versions say "a terra".

decisions.choice: "redentor" lowercase; deity_pronoun span on "ele"
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-2), the pronoun takes the setting because the most likely reading is that the redeemer is God himself (m2); the footnote gives the other view. The noun stays lowercase in Portuguese: it describes what this figure does for Job, the text does not name him, and the capital would decide the question that m2 leaves open more firmly than the setting does.

decisions.choice: goʾel as "ቤዢ" ("ቤዢዬ", my redeemer) at every level; Readable first says what he does, "የሚከላከልልኝ" (the one who will defend me), with "(ቤዢዬ)" after it
decisions.reason: "ቤዢ" is the word for the next-of-kin redeemer in Leviticus 25 and Ruth on main, so the reader can link Job's hope to the kinsman who buys back, avenges and defends a relative (meaning decision m1). "ታዳጊ" and "አዳኝ" say only "rescuer" and lose that link; "ታዳጊ" is also the Amharic of Acts 7:35 for a different Greek word. Readable follows the English Readable, which names the role and then the title. The wording is drafted from the Hebrew and does not follow an existing Amharic Bible.

decisions.choice: "በመጨረሻ" (at the last); "በአፈር ላይ ይቆማል" (L, B), "በምድር ላይ ቆሞ ይሟገትልኛል" (R)
decisions.reason: "በመጨረሻ" leaves open, as the meaning decision does, whether the Redeemer comes "in the end" or as the last to speak; "in the last day" would add a day of judgment that the Hebrew does not name. Literal and Balanced keep "the dust", which can be the earth or Job's grave; Readable says "the earth" and makes the courtroom sense plain with "ተሟገተ", the verb of Job's case elsewhere in the book.

decisions.choice: "छुटकारा दिलानेवाले" (L, B); "जो मेरा पक्ष लेंगे (मेरे छुटकारा दिलानेवाले)" (R)
decisions.reason: The go'el is the kinsman who stands up for a family member and buys him free (m1). "छुटकारा दिलानेवाला" is the form Psalm 19:14 gives the word, kept apart from "छुड़ानेवाला", the deliverer of other Hebrew words. Readable first says what he will do, as the English does.

decisions.choice: honorific "मेरे छुटकारा दिलानेवाले ... जीवित हैं", "वे ... खड़े होंगे"
alternatives: मेरा छुटकारा दिलानेवाला ... जीवित है, वह ... खड़ा होगा
decisions.reason: Hindi must choose plain or honorific agreement where English chooses a pronoun. The honorific follows the most likely reading, that the Redeemer is God himself (m2), as the English deity_pronoun span does; with the plain forms he would be a human kinsman.

decisions.choice: "धूल पर खड़े होंगे" (L, B); "धरती पर खड़े होकर मेरे पक्ष में बोलेंगे" (R)
decisions.reason: The verse is drafted from the Hebrew and its gloss, not from a familiar Hindi version: Literal and Balanced keep "the dust" (m4), which may mean the earth or Job's grave, and Readable says what standing up means, to speak for Job as in a court.

decisions.choice: "Искупитель", with a capital as the English level has it
decisions.reason: The go'el is the next of kin who buys back and stands up for a family member (m1); "искупитель" is the word Psalm 19:15 uses in this translation for the same Hebrew. The capital follows the English level and the reading that the Redeemer is God (m2), as the deity_pronoun span on "он" does. The line is drafted from the gloss, not from the Synodal.

decisions.choice: "последним"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word that can mean either "at the last" or "as the last one" (m3); Balanced and Readable say "в конце" as the English does.

decisions.choice: go'el "わたしを買い戻す方" (L), "わたしの贖い主" (B), "わたしを弁護してくださる方（わたしの贖い主）" (R), with respect forms ("生きておられ", "立たれる")
alternatives: "買い戻す者" at every level (as Ruth)
decisions.reason: In Ruth and the law the go'el is the kinsman who buys back land and family ("買い戻す者"); here the same kinsman's duty is turned to a court, where he stands up to defend and vindicate Job (m1, m4). Literal keeps that link with "買い戻す"; Balanced uses "贖い主", the title Japanese readers know for this verse, since a property sense would mislead; Readable says what he does and gives the title in brackets, as the English Readable does. The respect forms follow the reading that the go'el is most likely God himself (m2), which the footnote leaves open.

decisions.choice: "Викупитель" (L, B); Readable "той, хто мене захистить (мій Викупитель)", as the English gives the role and keeps the title
decisions.reason: The Job terms note asks for "Redeemer" at Literal and Balanced and the explained form at Readable; "Викупитель" keeps the kinsman's duty to buy back and to vindicate, which the meaning decisions leave open as to who he is.

source.text: וְאַחַ֣ר ע֭וֹרִֽי נִקְּפוּ־זֹ֑את וּ֝מִבְּשָׂרִ֗י אֶֽחֱזֶ֥ה אֱלֽוֹהַּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And after my skin they have struck off this, and from my flesh I will see God,

en.L: And after my skin has been struck off thus, \q and from my flesh I will see God,
en.B: And after my skin has been destroyed like this, \q yet in my flesh I will see God,
en.R: Even after my skin has been destroyed like this, \q I will see God with my own body.

es.L: Y después [que] mi piel haya sido arrancada así, \q y desde mi carne veré a Dios,
es.B: Y después que mi piel haya sido destruida de este modo, \q estando todavía en mi carne veré a Dios,
es.R: Aun después de que mi piel haya sido destruida así, \q veré a Dios con mi propio cuerpo.

fr.L: Et après que ma peau aura été arrachée ainsi, \q et depuis ma chair je verrai Dieu,
fr.B: Et quand ma peau aura été détruite de cette façon, \q c’est pourtant dans ma chair que je verrai Dieu,
fr.R: Même quand ma peau aura été détruite ainsi, \q je verrai Dieu dans mon propre corps.

sw.L: Na baada ya ngozi yangu kung'olewa hivi, \q na kutoka katika nyama yangu nitamwona Mungu,
sw.B: Na baada ya ngozi yangu kuharibiwa hivi, \q bado nikiwa katika mwili wangu nitamwona Mungu,
sw.R: Hata baada ya ngozi yangu kuharibiwa hivi, \q nitamwona Mungu kwa mwili wangu mwenyewe.

vi.L: Và sau khi da tôi bị lột đi như vầy, \q thì từ xác thịt tôi, tôi sẽ thấy Đức Chúa Trời,
vi.B: Và sau khi da tôi bị hủy hoại như thế, \q thì trong chính thân xác mình, tôi vẫn sẽ thấy Đức Chúa Trời,
vi.R: Dù sau khi da tôi bị hủy hoại như thế, \q tôi vẫn sẽ thấy Đức Chúa Trời bằng chính thân thể mình.

ko.L: 내 가죽이 이렇게 벗겨진 후에도, \q 내가 내 육체로부터 하나님을 뵐 것이다.
ko.B: 내 살갗이 이렇게 다 망가진 뒤에도, \q 나는 이 몸으로 하나님을 뵐 것이다.
ko.R: 이렇게 내 살갗이 다 망가진 뒤에라도, \q 나는 내 몸으로 하나님을 뵐 것이다.

pt.L: E depois que a minha pele for assim arrancada, \q e da minha carne verei a Deus,
pt.B: E, depois que a minha pele tiver sido destruída assim, \q eu verei a Deus na minha carne,
pt.R: Mesmo depois que a minha pele tiver sido destruída desse jeito, \q eu verei a Deus no meu próprio corpo.

am.L: ቆዳዬም እንዲህ ከተገፈፈ በኋላ፣ \q ከሥጋዬም አምላክን አያለሁ፣
am.B: ቆዳዬ እንዲህ ከጠፋ በኋላ እንኳ፣ \q በገዛ ሥጋዬ አምላክን አያለሁ፣
am.R: ቆዳዬ እንዲህ ከጠፋ በኋላ እንኳ፣ \q በገዛ ሰውነቴ አምላክን አያለሁ።

hi.L: और मेरी खाल के इस प्रकार उतार दिए जाने के बाद, \q और अपनी देह से मैं परमेश्वर को देखूँगा,
hi.B: और जब मेरी खाल इस तरह उधेड़ दी जा चुकी होगी, \q तब भी अपनी देह में रहते हुए मैं परमेश्वर को देखूँगा,
hi.R: मेरी खाल इस तरह नष्ट हो जाने के बाद भी \q मैं अपनी इसी देह के साथ परमेश्वर को देखूँगा।

ru.L: И после того как кожа моя будет так содрана, \q и из моей плоти я увижу Бога,
ru.B: И когда моя кожа будет вот так разрушена, \q всё же в своём теле я увижу Бога,
ru.R: Даже когда моя кожа будет вот так уничтожена, \q я увижу Бога, оставаясь в своём теле.

ja.L: わたしの皮膚がこのように打ち砕かれた後、 \q わたしは自分の肉から神を見るだろう。
ja.B: わたしの皮膚がこのように滅ぼされた後も、 \q わたしはこの肉において神を見るだろう。
ja.R: わたしの皮膚がこのように滅ぼされた後でも、 \q わたしは自分のこの体で、神を見るのだ。

uk.L: І після того, як мою шкіру так здеруть, \q то з мого тіла я побачу Бога,
uk.B: І після того, як мою шкіру так знищать, \q то все ж у своєму тілі я побачу Бога,
uk.R: Навіть після того, як мою шкіру так знищено, \q я побачу Бога у своєму власному тілі.

decisions.choice: after my skin has been struck off thus: after my body is destroyed
alternatives: after I awake, he will set me up
after my skin, this (body) is struck off
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is very compressed: "and after my skin, they have struck off this". It most likely means "after my skin has been destroyed like this", either by the disease that is eating him now (verse 20; 2:7) or in death. The words have been read in several other ways.

decisions.choice: from my flesh: in my flesh, from within my body
alternatives: without my flesh, apart from my body
decisions.reason: The word "from" can mean "from within" (seeing God from inside his body) or "away from" (seeing God after he has left his body). Verse 27 stresses Job's own eyes, which favors "in my flesh": Job expects to see God as himself, in his body, whether before his death or after it. The other reading is that Job will see God after death, without his body.

decisions.choice: I will see God: face to face
decisions.reason: The verb (chazah) is to see or behold. Job longs to meet God in person and be heard (13:15-16; 23:3-7); at the end of the book he says, "now my eye sees you" (42:5).

decisions.choice: in my flesh (B), with my own body (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the more likely reading (m2); Literal keeps the open "from".

decisions.choice: "depuis ma chair" at Literal
decisions.reason: Like the Hebrew "from", "depuis" leaves open whether Job sees God from within his body or after leaving it (meaning decision m2); Balanced and Readable follow the more likely reading, "dans ma chair".

decisions.choice: "뵐 것이다", the humble verb for seeing a superior
decisions.reason: Korean uses the humble form for meeting God, which fits Job's longing to come before him (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: "da minha carne" (L); "na minha carne" (B); "no meu próprio corpo" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the open preposition: "da minha carne" can be seen from within the body or away from it, as the Hebrew "from" can (m2). Balanced and Readable follow the more likely reading, in his own body; the other reading, "fora da minha carne", seeing God after death without the body, is in the meaning note and its footnote. The first line follows the most likely sense of a compressed Hebrew phrase (m1).

decisions.choice: "ከሥጋዬ" (from my flesh) at Literal; "በገዛ ሥጋዬ" (B), "በገዛ ሰውነቴ" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "from", which can mean from within the body or away from it (meaning decision m2). Balanced and Readable follow the reading the meaning decision favours, "in my flesh", as the English does. Eloah is "አምላክ", as elsewhere in Job.

decisions.choice: "अपनी देह से"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the open preposition (m2): Hindi "से" can mean from within the body or apart from it, as the Hebrew can. Balanced and Readable follow the more likely reading, in the body, as the English does.

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֲנִ֨י׀אֶֽחֱזֶה־לִּ֗י וְעֵינַ֣י רָא֣וּ וְלֹא־זָ֑ר כָּל֖וּ כִלְיֹתַ֣י בְּחֵקִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: whom I, I will see for myself, and my eyes will see, and not a stranger; are spent my kidneys in my bosom.

en.L: whom I myself will see for myself, \q and my eyes will see, and not a stranger. \q My kidneys are spent within me.
en.B: whom I myself will see on my side, \q whom my own eyes will behold, and not as a stranger. \q My heart faints within me!
en.R: I will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for myself. \q I will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with my own eyes, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not be a stranger to me. \q I long for that day with all my heart.

es.L: a quien yo mismo veré para mí, \q y mis ojos [lo] verán, y no un extraño. \q Mis riñones se consumen dentro de mí.
es.B: a quien yo mismo veré de mi parte, \q a quien mis propios ojos contemplarán, y no como a un extraño. \q ¡Mi corazón desfallece dentro de mí!
es.R: Yo mismo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} veré. \q Con mis propios ojos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} veré, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no será un extraño para mí. \q ¡Con todo el corazón anhelo ese día!

fr.L: celui que je verrai, moi, pour moi, \q et que mes yeux verront, et non un étranger. \q Mes reins se consument au-dedans de moi.
fr.B: {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que je verrai moi-même à mes côtés, \q que mes propres yeux contempleront, et non comme un étranger. \q Mon cœur défaille au-dedans de moi !
fr.R: Je {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} verrai moi-même. \q Je {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} verrai de mes propres yeux, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne sera pas un étranger pour moi. \q De tout mon cœur, j’attends ce jour-là.

sw.L: ambaye mimi nitamwona kwa ajili yangu, \q na macho yangu yatamwona, wala si mgeni. \q Figo zangu zimezimia ndani yangu.
sw.B: ambaye mimi mwenyewe nitamwona upande wangu, \q ambaye macho yangu mwenyewe yatamtazama, wala si kama mgeni. \q Moyo wangu unazimia ndani yangu!
sw.R: Nitamwona mimi mwenyewe. \q Nitamwona kwa macho yangu mwenyewe, wala {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hatakuwa mgeni kwangu. \q Ninaitamani siku hiyo kwa moyo wangu wote.

vi.L: Đấng mà chính tôi sẽ thấy cho tôi, \q và mắt tôi sẽ thấy, chứ không phải người lạ. \q Ruột gan tôi hao mòn trong tôi.
vi.B: chính tôi sẽ thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đứng về phía tôi, \q chính mắt tôi sẽ nhìn thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, không như một người xa lạ. \q Lòng tôi mòn mỏi khát khao!
vi.R: Chính tôi sẽ thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Tôi sẽ thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} tận mắt, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ không còn xa lạ với tôi. \q Tôi hết lòng mong mỏi ngày đó.

ko.L: 그분을 내가 친히 나를 위하여 뵐 것이요, \q 내 눈이 [그분을] 뵐 것이니, 낯선 이가 아니다. \q 내 콩팥이 내 속에서 쇠약해진다.
ko.B: 내가 친히 내 편이 되신 그분을 뵐 것이요, \q 내 눈으로 그분을 뵐 것이니, 낯선 분으로 뵙지 않을 것이다. \q 내 마음이 속에서 타들어 간다!
ko.R: 내가 직접 그분을 뵐 것이다. \q 내 눈으로 그분을 뵐 것이고, 그분은 나에게 낯선 분이 아닐 것이다. \q 나는 온 마음으로 그날을 간절히 기다린다.

pt.L: a quem eu mesmo verei para mim, \q e os meus olhos verão, e não um estranho. \q Os meus rins se consomem dentro de mim.
pt.B: a quem eu mesmo verei do meu lado, \q a quem os meus próprios olhos contemplarão, e não como um estranho. \q O meu coração se consome dentro de mim!
pt.R: Eu mesmo {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} verei. \q Eu {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} verei com os meus próprios olhos, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} não será um estranho para mim. \q Desejo esse dia de todo o coração.

am.L: እርሱን እኔ ራሴ ለራሴ አየዋለሁ፤ \q ዓይኖቼም ያዩታል፤ እንግዳም አይደለም። \q ኩላሊቶቼ በውስጤ ዛሉ።
am.B: እርሱን እኔ ራሴ ከጎኔ ሆኖ አየዋለሁ፤ \q በገዛ ዓይኖቼ እመለከተዋለሁ፤ እንደ እንግዳም አይሆንብኝም። \q ልቤ በውስጤ ዛለ!
am.R: እኔ ራሴ አየዋለሁ። \q በገዛ ዓይኖቼ አየዋለሁ፤ ለእኔም እንግዳ አይሆንብኝም። \q ያንን ቀን በሙሉ ልቤ እናፍቃለሁ።

hi.L: जिन्हें मैं स्वयं अपने लिए देखूँगा, \q और मेरी आँखें देखेंगी, और कोई पराया नहीं। \q मेरे भीतर मेरे गुर्दे क्षीण हो गए हैं।
hi.B: जिन्हें मैं स्वयं अपने पक्ष में देखूँगा, \q जिन्हें मेरी अपनी आँखें निहारेंगी, और पराए के रूप में नहीं। \q मेरा मन मेरे भीतर तरसते-तरसते हार चला है!
hi.R: मैं ख़ुद उन्हें देखूँगा। \q मैं अपनी ही आँखों से उन्हें देखूँगा, और वे मेरे लिए पराए नहीं होंगे। \q उस दिन के लिए मैं पूरे मन से तरसता हूँ।

ru.L: которого я сам увижу для себя, \q и мои глаза увидят, и не чужой. \q Истощились мои почки внутри меня.
ru.B: которого я сам увижу на своей стороне, \q которого увидят мои собственные глаза, и не как чужого. \q Изнемогает сердце во мне!
ru.R: Я сам увижу {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}. \q Я увижу {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} своими глазами, и {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} не будет мне чужим. \q Всем сердцем я жду этого дня.

ja.L: わたし自身が、わたしのためにその方を見る。 \q わたしの目が見るのであって、ほかの者ではない。 \q わたしの腎臓は、わたしのうちで衰え果てる。
ja.B: そのわたし自身が、わたしの味方として、その方を見る。 \q わたし自身の目が見るのだ。よそよそしい方としてではなく。 \q わたしの心は、うちで衰え果てる！
ja.R: わたしは、自分でその方を見る。 \q 自分の目でその方を見る。その方は、わたしにとって見知らぬ方ではない。 \q わたしは、その日を心から待ち焦がれている。

uk.L: якого я сам побачу для себе, \q і мої очі побачать, а не чужий. \q Мої нирки знемагають у мені.
uk.B: якого я сам побачу на своєму боці, \q якого мої власні очі побачать, і не як чужого. \q Моє серце млоїть у мені!
uk.R: Я побачу {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} сам. \q Я побачу {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} на власні очі, і {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} не буде мені чужим. \q Усім серцем я прагну того дня.

decisions.choice: for myself: for my good, on my side
decisions.reason: The words "for me" can mean that Job will see God himself, or that he will see God on his side, no longer against him. Both senses fit after verse 25.

decisions.choice: not a stranger: God will not be a stranger to Job
alternatives: I, and not another, will see him
decisions.reason: "And not a stranger" can describe God, who will no longer be an outsider or an enemy to Job (verses 13-15 used the same word of Job's family), or it can stress that Job himself, not someone else, will see God.

decisions.choice: my kidneys are spent within me: I long for it with all my heart
decisions.reason: The kidneys stand for the inmost feelings (Psalm 73:21; Proverbs 23:16). To be "spent" or to faint is to long with all one's strength (Psalm 84:3; 119:81).

decisions.choice: my heart (B), with all my heart (R)
decisions.reason: English speaks of the heart, not the kidneys, as the seat of the feelings (m3).

decisions.choice: not as a stranger
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the first reading of m2; the footnote gives the other.

decisions.choice: a deity_pronoun span on the relative "lui que" at Balanced
alternatives: "celui que" with no span, as at Literal
decisions.reason: Balanced opens the line with the pronoun "lui", which refers to God (verse 26), so it takes the setting; Literal says "celui que", which takes none.

decisions.choice: "ruột gan" (bowels and liver) for the kidneys
decisions.reason: Vietnamese speaks of the inmost feelings as "ruột gan", as Hebrew does with the kidneys (meaning decision m3); "thận" would read as a plain organ.

decisions.choice: "እንግዳም አይደለም" (and not a stranger); "ኩላሊቶቼ በውስጤ ዛሉ" (my kidneys are spent within me)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "እንግዳ", the word used of Job's estranged household in verses 13-15, and leaves open, as the Hebrew does, whether it is God who will no longer be a stranger or Job who, and no other, will see him (meaning decision m2); "ሌላ" (another) would choose the second reading. The kidneys stay at Literal; Balanced says "heart", the Amharic seat of longing.

decisions.choice: "मेरा मन" (B), "पूरे मन से" (R); Literal "मेरे गुर्दे"
decisions.reason: Hindi, like English, speaks of the heart or mind, not the kidneys, as the seat of longing (m3); Literal keeps the Hebrew organ.

decisions.choice: "сердце" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Russian, like English, speaks of the heart as the seat of the feelings (m3); Literal keeps the kidneys.

decisions.choice: the relative "whom" that ties verse 27 to "God" in verse 26 becomes a new sentence with "その方を見る"
alternatives: one sentence over 26-27 ("……神を、わたし自身が見る")
decisions.reason: A Japanese relative clause would have to come before "神" in verse 26 and pull verse 27's content across the verse boundary; "その方" keeps each verse's words after its own number.

source.text: כִּ֣י תֹ֭אמְרוּמַה־נִּרְדָּף־ל֑וֹ וְשֹׁ֥רֶשׁ דָּ֝בָ֗ר נִמְצָא־בִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: For you say, How we will pursue him! and [the] root of [the] matter is found in me,

en.L: If you say, "How we will pursue him!" \q and [that] the root of the matter is found in me,
en.B: If you say, "How we will hound him!" \q and that the root of the trouble lies in me,
en.R: You may say, "Let us keep after him!" \q You may say that I caused my own trouble.

es.L: Si {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «¡Cómo lo perseguiremos!», \q y [que] la raíz del asunto se halla en mí,
es.B: Si {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: «¡Cómo lo vamos a acosar!», \q y que la raíz del mal está en mí,
es.R: Tal vez {{plural_you:digan|digáis}}: «¡Sigamos acosándolo!». \q Tal vez {{plural_you:digan|digáis}} que yo mismo causé mis problemas.

fr.L: Si vous dites : « Comme nous le poursuivrons ! » \q et [que] la racine de l’affaire se trouve en moi,
fr.B: Si vous dites : « Comme nous allons le traquer ! » \q et que la racine du mal se trouve en moi,
fr.R: Vous direz peut-être : « Continuons à le harceler ! » \q Vous direz peut-être que c’est moi qui suis la cause de mes malheurs.

sw.L: Mkisema, "Jinsi tutakavyomfuatia!" \q na [kwamba] shina la jambo linapatikana ndani yangu,
sw.B: Mkisema, "Jinsi tutakavyomwandama!" \q na kwamba chanzo cha taabu kiko ndani yangu,
sw.R: Huenda mkasema, "Tuendelee kumwandama!" \q Huenda mkasema kwamba mimi mwenyewe nimesababisha taabu zangu.

vi.L: Nếu các anh nói: "Chúng ta sẽ bắt bớ hắn thế nào!" \q và [rằng] gốc rễ của sự việc ở nơi tôi,
vi.B: Nếu các anh nói: "Chúng ta sẽ truy đuổi hắn biết bao!" \q và rằng căn nguyên của tai họa nằm nơi tôi,
vi.R: Các anh có thể nói: "Hãy cứ bám theo hắn!" \q Các anh có thể nói rằng chính tôi đã gây ra tai họa cho mình.

ko.L: 그대들이 "우리가 그를 얼마나 쫓을 것인가!" 하고, \q 일의 뿌리가 내게 있다고 말한다면,
ko.B: 그대들이 "우리가 그를 끝까지 몰아붙이자!" 하며, \q 재앙의 뿌리가 내게 있다고 말한다면,
ko.R: 그대들은 "계속 그를 몰아붙이자!" 하고 말할지도 모르오. \q 내가 스스로 화를 불렀다고 말할지도 모르오.

pt.L: Se vocês dizem: "Como o perseguiremos!" \q e [que] a raiz da questão se acha em mim,
pt.B: Se vocês dizem: "Como vamos acossá-lo!" \q e que a raiz do problema está em mim,
pt.R: Vocês podem dizer: "Vamos continuar em cima dele!" \q Podem dizer que eu mesmo causei a minha desgraça.

am.L: «እንዴት እናሳድደዋለን!» ብትሉ፣ \q የነገሩም ሥር በእኔ ተገኝቷል ብትሉ፣
am.B: «እንዴት አድርገን እናሳድደዋለን!» ብትሉ፣ \q የችግሩም ሥር በእኔ ነው ብትሉ፣
am.R: «ማሳደዳችንን እንቀጥል!» ትሉ ይሆናል። \q ችግሬን ያመጣሁት ራሴ ነኝ ትሉ ይሆናል።

hi.L: यदि तुम कहो, "हम उसका कैसा पीछा करेंगे!" \q और [यह कि] बात की जड़ मुझमें पाई जाती है,
hi.B: यदि तुम कहो, "हम उसके पीछे कैसे पड़ेंगे!" \q और यह कि मुसीबत की जड़ मुझमें ही है,
hi.R: तुम शायद कहो, "चलो, उसके पीछे पड़े रहें!" \q तुम शायद कहो कि अपनी मुसीबत का कारण मैं ख़ुद हूँ।

ru.L: Если вы скажете: «Как мы будем преследовать его!» — \q и [что] корень дела найден во мне,
ru.B: Если вы скажете: «Как мы будем травить его!» — \q и что корень беды во мне,
ru.R: Вы можете сказать: «Не будем отступать от него!» \q Вы можете сказать, что я сам виноват в своей беде.

ja.L: もしあなたがたが「どこまでも彼を追いかけよう！」と言い、 \q 事の根はわたしの中に見いだされる、と[言う]なら、
ja.B: もし、あなたがたが「どこまでも彼を追い詰めてやろう！」と言い、 \q 苦しみの根はわたしにある、と言うなら、
ja.R: あなたたちは「あいつを追い詰め続けよう！」と言うかもしれない。 \q わたしが自分で苦しみを招いたのだ、と言うかもしれない。

uk.L: Якщо ви кажете: «Як ми переслідуватимемо його!» \q і [що] корінь справи знайдено в мені,
uk.B: Якщо ви кажете: «Як ми його цькуватимемо!» \q і що корінь біди — в мені,
uk.R: Ви можете сказати: «Не відступаймося від нього!» \q Ви можете сказати, що я сам накликав на себе біду.

decisions.choice: if you say: a condition completed in verse 29
decisions.reason: The opening word introduces a condition; verse 29 gives its outcome: then fear the sword.

decisions.choice: in me
decisions.reason: The Leningrad Codex reads "in me": Job reports the friends' claim in his own words. Many Hebrew manuscripts and the ancient translations read "in him", which makes the words a direct quotation of the friends. The meaning is the same: the friends say the cause of Job's suffering is Job himself.

decisions.choice: the root of the matter: the cause of the trouble
decisions.reason: The "root" is the cause or source. The friends say Job's suffering comes from his own sin (4:7-8; 8:4; 11:6).

decisions.choice: how we will pursue him!: the friends' resolve to keep after Job
alternatives: what will we pursue in him?
decisions.reason: The words can be an exclamation, "how we will hound him!", or a question, "what charge will we bring against him?" Either way the friends mean to keep accusing Job.

source.text: גּ֤וּרוּ לָכֶ֨ם׀מִפְּנֵי־חֶ֗רֶב כִּֽי־חֵ֭מָה עֲוֺנ֣וֹת חָ֑רֶב לְמַ֖עַן תֵּדְע֣וּן שַׁדּֽוּן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Be afraid for yourselves of [the] face of [the] sword, for wrath [is the] iniquities of [the] sword, so that you may know [there is] a judgment.

en.L: be afraid for yourselves of the sword, \q for wrath [brings] the punishments of the sword, \q so that you may know [that there is] a judgment.
en.B: be afraid of the sword yourselves, \q for wrath brings the punishment of the sword, \q so that you may know that there is judgment.
en.R: But you should be afraid of the sword yourselves. \q God punishes such wrongs with the sword in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger. \q Then you will know that there is judgment.

es.L: {{plural_you:teman|temed}} por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos la espada, \q porque la ira [trae] los castigos de la espada, \q para que {{plural_you:sepan|sepáis}} [que hay] un juicio.
es.B: {{plural_you:teman|temed}} {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos la espada, \q porque la ira trae el castigo de la espada, \q para que {{plural_you:sepan|sepáis}} que hay juicio.
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} mismos {{plural_you:deberían|deberíais}} temer la espada. \q Dios castiga esas maldades con la espada en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira. \q Entonces {{plural_you:sabrán|sabréis}} que hay juicio.

fr.L: craignez pour vous-mêmes l’épée, \q car la colère [amène] les châtiments de l’épée, \q afin que vous sachiez [qu’il y a] un jugement.
fr.B: craignez vous-mêmes l’épée, \q car la colère amène le châtiment de l’épée, \q afin que vous sachiez qu’il y a un jugement.
fr.R: Mais c’est vous qui devriez avoir peur de l’épée. \q Dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère, Dieu punit ces fautes par l’épée. \q Alors vous saurez qu’il y a un jugement.

sw.L: ogopeni upanga kwa ajili yenu wenyewe, \q kwa maana ghadhabu [huleta] adhabu za upanga, \q ili mpate kujua [kwamba kuna] hukumu.
sw.B: ninyi wenyewe uogopeni upanga, \q kwa maana ghadhabu huleta adhabu ya upanga, \q ili mjue kwamba kuna hukumu.
sw.R: Lakini ninyi wenyewe mnapaswa kuuogopa upanga. \q Mungu huadhibu makosa kama hayo kwa upanga katika hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. \q Ndipo mtakapojua kwamba kuna hukumu.

vi.L: thì chính các anh hãy sợ gươm, \q vì cơn thịnh nộ [mang lại] những hình phạt của gươm, \q để các anh biết [rằng có] sự phán xét.
vi.B: thì chính các anh hãy sợ lưỡi gươm, \q vì cơn thịnh nộ đem đến hình phạt bằng gươm, \q để các anh biết rằng có sự phán xét.
vi.R: Nhưng chính các anh mới phải sợ lưỡi gươm. \q Đức Chúa Trời dùng gươm trừng phạt những tội như thế trong cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Lúc ấy các anh sẽ biết là có sự phán xét.

ko.L: 그대들 스스로 칼을 두려워하시오. \q 진노는 칼의 형벌을 [가져오니], \q 그대들이 심판이 [있음을] 알게 될 것이오.
ko.B: 그대들 자신이 칼을 두려워해야 하오. \q 진노가 칼의 형벌을 불러오니, \q 그대들은 심판이 있음을 알게 될 것이오.
ko.R: 오히려 그대들이 칼을 두려워해야 하오. \q 하나님께서 진노하셔서 그런 잘못을 칼로 벌하실 것이오. \q 그때 그대들은 심판이 있음을 알게 될 것이오.

pt.L: temam por vocês mesmos diante da espada, \q pois a ira [traz] os castigos da espada, \q para que saibam [que há] um julgamento.
pt.B: tenham medo da espada vocês mesmos, \q pois a ira traz o castigo da espada, \q para que saibam que há julgamento.
pt.R: Mas vocês é que deveriam ter medo da espada. \q Na {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} ira, Deus castiga esses erros com a espada. \q Então vocês vão saber que existe julgamento.

am.L: ከሰይፍ ፊት ለራሳችሁ ፍሩ፤ \q ቁጣ የሰይፍን ቅጣት [ያመጣል]ና፤ \q ፍርድ እንዳለ ታውቁ ዘንድ።
am.B: እናንተ ራሳችሁ ሰይፍን ፍሩ፤ \q ቁጣ የሰይፍን ቅጣት ያመጣልና፤ \q ይህም ፍርድ እንዳለ ታውቁ ዘንድ ነው።
am.R: ይልቁንስ እናንተ ራሳችሁ ሰይፍን ፍሩ። \q እግዚአብሔር እንዲህ ያለውን በደል በቁጣው በሰይፍ ይቀጣል። \q ያን ጊዜ ፍርድ እንዳለ ታውቃላችሁ።

hi.L: तो अपने लिए तलवार से डरो, \q क्योंकि क्रोध तलवार के दंड [लाता है], \q ताकि तुम जान लो [कि] न्याय [होता है]।
hi.B: तो तुम स्वयं तलवार से डरो, \q क्योंकि क्रोध तलवार का दंड लाता है, \q ताकि तुम जान लो कि न्याय होता है।
hi.R: पर तुम्हें ख़ुद तलवार से डरना चाहिए। \q परमेश्वर अपने क्रोध में ऐसे अपराधों का दंड तलवार से देते हैं। \q तब तुम जानोगे कि न्याय होता है।

ru.L: бойтесь для себя меча, \q ведь гнев [навлекает] кары меча, \q чтобы вы знали, [что есть] суд.
ru.B: бойтесь меча сами, \q ведь гнев навлекает кару меча, \q чтобы вы знали, что есть суд.
ru.R: Но вы сами должны бояться меча. \q Бог в своём гневе наказывает за такое зло мечом. \q Тогда вы узнаете, что есть суд.

ja.L: 自分のために剣を恐れるがよい。 \q 憤りは剣の刑罰[をもたらす]からだ。 \q そうして、あなたがたは裁きが[ある]ことを知るだろう。
ja.B: あなたがた自身こそ、剣を恐れるがよい。 \q 憤りは剣による罰をもたらす。 \q そうすれば、裁きがあることを知るだろう。
ja.R: でも、あなたたちこそ、剣を恐れるべきだ。 \q 神は怒って、そのような悪を剣で罰せられる。 \q そのとき、裁きがあることを知るだろう。

uk.L: бійтеся собі меча, \q бо гнів [приносить] покарання мечем, \q щоб ви знали, [що є] суд.
uk.B: то самі бійтеся меча, \q бо гнів несе покарання мечем, \q щоб ви знали, що є суд.
uk.R: Але вам самим слід боятися меча. \q Бог у своєму гніві карає такі провини мечем. \q Тоді ви знатимете, що є суд.

decisions.choice: the sword: God's judgment turned on the friends
decisions.reason: Job warns the friends that God will judge them for the way they have spoken about him (13:7-11). At the end of the book God's anger burns against the friends (42:7-8).

decisions.choice: wrath brings the punishments of the sword
alternatives: wrath is (one of) the sins that deserve the sword
decisions.reason: The line is compressed: "for wrath, iniquities of the sword". The word for iniquity can also mean its punishment.
